model_interpretation.claim: Keeping the baseline 128-thread shared-memory reduction tree while storing every partial in int64 should preserve exact cancellation behavior. A bounded finalizer handles up to 1024 partials; larger arrays get parallel reduction stages. This adaptive topology may reduce full-call cost by avoiding recursive work and the final copy for ordinary sizes, while not assigning the full large input to one CTA. It remains a performance hypothesis until measured.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.cu"],"retained":["Generalized the baseline reduction kernel to read int values into int64 accumulators while retaining its 128-thread shared-memory tree.","Added a direct exact one-CTA path for up to 128 values; for larger inputs, first emits 128-value int64 partials into scratch.","Finalizes at most 1024 partials in one CTA writing directly to out; recursively adds parallel 128-way partial stages above that bound using two packed scratch buffers.","Uses no scratch reads before writes and launches work on the default stream; narrows to int only after the true total is formed."]}

model_interpretation.claim: A warp-shuffle reduction followed by one shared exchange of four warp partials should reduce CTA-wide synchronization from the baseline tree’s repeated barriers to one per block. The recursive 128-element pass geometry stays fixed; 64-bit partials prevent overflow in intermediate groups when the valid final sum fits int. Added wide arithmetic and scratch traffic could offset the synchronization savings, so no whole-call speedup is assumed.
